dct_description_sm: It is well known that Inuit children from Canada, United States and Greenland suffer from high incidence of respiratory infections, and many authors have identified higher rates of ear infections and lower respiratory tract infections in Inuit, compared to control Caucasian populations. We investigated the relation between maternal organochlorines (OCs) concentrations and acute respiratory and gastro-intestinal infections in a cohort of 199 infants of the same population. The number of subjects was however small, and the associations were not always statistically significant. Therefore, we decided to clarify the possible link between prenatal exposure to OCs and infections in this population. The aim of this study was to identify an association between prenatal exposure to OCs and acute respiratory infections during the first five years of life.   Specific objectives were: 1) To determine the incidence of infectious diseases during the first 5 years of life, and 2) To assess the impact of prenatal exposure to OCs on the incidence of infections.

dct_title_s: Effects of Exposure to Organochlorines on the Infectious Diseases Incidence of Inuit Preschool Children
